lines.t: Do you know where the nearest printer is?

options: Yes, I printed it this morning.
There's one on the second floor of the library.
It's about ten pages long.
No, I'm not near it.
optionNotes: Repeats 'print' but says nothing about where a printer is.
Correct: it gives a location, which is what the question asks for.
Answers 'how long is it?', not 'where?'.
Plays on 'nearest/near' but doesn't answer the question.
questions.explanation: The speaker wants a location. Only B gives a place (second floor of the library). The other options reuse words from the question (print, near) without answering it.

lines.t: What time does the dining hall close on Sundays?

options: At eight, I think. That's earlier than on weekdays.
It's right next to the gym.
I usually have pasta there.
Yes, it was closed last Sunday.
optionNotes: Correct: gives a time, answering 'what time'.
Answers 'where', not 'what time'.
Talks about food, not closing time.
A yes/no answer to a wh-question, and in the wrong tense.
questions.explanation: 'What time' requires a time. Only A gives one. B answers 'where', C is off-topic and D answers a yes/no question about the past.

lines.t: Would you mind if I borrowed your notes from Tuesday's lecture?

options: No, I didn't mind the lecture at all.
Tuesday works better for me.
Not at all. I'll email them to you tonight.
I borrowed them from the library.
optionNotes: Repeats 'mind' and 'lecture' but answers a different question.
Treats the request as a scheduling question.
Correct: 'Not at all' means 'I don't mind', so it accepts the request.
Repeats 'borrowed' but doesn't respond to the request.
questions.explanation: 'Would you mind if...?' is a polite request; 'Not at all' grants permission. C agrees and adds a helpful detail. Remember: answering 'Yes' to 'Would you mind' would actually mean refusing.

lines.t: I can't believe the professor moved the exam up a whole week.

options: I know. I'll have to rethink my entire study schedule.
It's on the third floor, up the stairs.
Yes, I believe he's a full professor.
A week should be enough to move everything.
optionNotes: Correct: shares the speaker's surprise and reacts to having less time.
Misreads 'moved up' as a physical location.
Repeats 'believe' and 'professor' but ignores the complaint.
Misreads 'move' as moving belongings.
questions.explanation: 'Move something up' means make it earlier. The speaker is complaining, so a sympathetic reaction about losing study time (A) fits. B and D take 'move' literally; C just echoes words.

lines.t: How long does it take to get to campus by bus?

options: The bus is blue and white.
It costs two dollars each way.
I took it yesterday afternoon.
About twenty minutes if there's no traffic.
optionNotes: Describes the bus, not the travel time.
Answers 'how much', not 'how long'.
Says when the speaker took it, not how long it takes.
Correct: gives a duration.
questions.explanation: 'How long does it take' asks for a duration. Only D gives one. B is a classic trap: it answers 'how much'.

lines.t: Why don't we grab lunch after the seminar?

options: Because the seminar ends at noon.
Sounds good. How about that new Thai place?
I didn't grab anything.
The seminar was really interesting.
optionNotes: Treats 'Why don't we' as a real question about reasons.
Correct: accepts the invitation and suggests a place.
Repeats 'grab' with a different meaning.
Comments on the seminar instead of the invitation.
questions.explanation: 'Why don't we...?' is an invitation, not a request for a reason. B accepts naturally. A answers with 'because', which is the trap.

lines.t: Has anyone told you the lab report's been pushed back to Friday?

options: No, it hasn't been pushed out of the lab.
I reported it to the lab manager on Friday.
Really? That's a relief. I'm nowhere near done.
Friday's lab is in room 204.
optionNotes: Takes 'pushed' literally.
Repeats 'report' and 'Friday' with a different meaning.
Correct: reacts to the news that the deadline is later.
Gives a location that nobody asked for.
questions.explanation: 'Pushed back' means postponed. The speaker is sharing news, so a reaction like C ('That's a relief') is natural. The other options recycle words (pushed, report, Friday, lab).

lines.t: Excuse me, is this seat taken?

options: Yes, I took the bus today.
It's a really comfortable chair.
I'm taking four classes this term.
No, go right ahead.
optionNotes: Repeats 'took/taken' with a different meaning.
Describes the seat but doesn't say whether it is free.
Repeats 'taking' with a different meaning.
Correct: the seat is free, so the speaker can sit.
questions.explanation: 'Is this seat taken?' asks if someone is using it. 'No, go right ahead' says it is free and invites the person to sit.

lines.t: I was hoping you could look over my cover letter sometime this week.

options: Sure, I'll send you my cover letter tomorrow.
I'd be happy to. Is Thursday soon enough?
I hope the letter covers everything.
It was a pretty long letter, wasn't it?
optionNotes: Reverses the roles: the speaker wants the listener to read HER letter.
Correct: accepts the request and proposes a time.
Repeats 'hope' and 'cover' but doesn't respond to the request.
Talks about a letter as if it had already been read.
questions.explanation: 'I was hoping you could...' is an indirect request for help. B accepts and offers a day. A is a role-reversal trap.

lines.t: Where should I drop off the equipment I borrowed?

options: At the media desk on the ground floor.
You can borrow it for up to three days.
I dropped it last week by accident.
Whenever it's convenient for you.
optionNotes: Correct: gives a place to return it.
Answers 'how long can I borrow it?'.
Repeats 'drop' with a different meaning.
Answers 'when', not 'where'.
questions.explanation: The question asks 'where'. Only A gives a place. D is the wrong wh-word trap (when); C plays on 'drop'.

lines.t: You're not still working on that essay, are you?

options: No, I'm not working at the café anymore.
The essay is about climate policy.
I wish I weren't. The conclusion is giving me trouble.
You can still turn it in on time.
optionNotes: Changes 'working' to mean a job.
Answers 'what is it about?'.
Correct: indirectly says 'yes, I'm still working on it' and explains why.
Sounds like advice to the speaker, who isn't the one writing the essay.
questions.explanation: The speaker is surprised the listener is still working. 'I wish I weren't' means 'Yes, unfortunately I am', which answers the question indirectly.

lines.t: Can you tell me how to get to the registrar's office?

options: I registered for my classes online.
The office closes at five on Fridays.
Sure. It's in the admin building, just past the fountain.
Yes, I can tell you're new here.
optionNotes: Plays on 'registrar/registered'.
Gives opening hours, not directions.
Correct: gives directions.
Repeats 'tell' with a different meaning.
questions.explanation: The speaker is asking for directions. C gives them. A and D reuse sounds from the question; B answers a different question.
